drafted_by: AI, requires clinician review before any real use.

questions.text: What is bothering you in your mouth: tooth pain, gum problems, sores, swelling, dry mouth, taste changes, or something else?
questions.rationale: Clarifying the main oral complaint guides the next branch of the interview.

questions.text: Where is the tooth pain, and is it sharp, throbbing, or triggered by hot, cold, sweet, or chewing?
questions.rationale: Pain pattern helps separate pulpitis, abscess, cracked tooth, and sensitivity.

questions.text: When did this start, and is it getting better, worse, or staying the same?
questions.rationale: Onset and trajectory distinguish acute infection from chronic problems.

questions.text: Is there swelling in your face, cheek, jaw, or under your tongue?
questions.rationale: Swelling suggests a dental abscess or spreading odontogenic infection.

questions.text: Do you have trouble opening your mouth, swallowing, or controlling saliva?
questions.rationale: Trismus, dysphagia, or drooling can signal deep space infection threatening the airway.

questions.text: Is your tongue, lip, or throat swelling, or is it hard to breathe?
questions.rationale: Swelling with breathing difficulty may be angioedema or infection and is an emergency.

questions.text: Have you had fever, chills, or felt generally unwell?
questions.rationale: Systemic symptoms indicate spreading infection.

questions.text: Do your gums bleed, look swollen or red, or have they been pulling away from your teeth?
questions.rationale: These are signs of gingivitis or periodontitis.

questions.text: Do you have any sores or ulcers in your mouth? How many, and do they come and go?
questions.rationale: Recurrent aphthae differ from persistent ulcers or systemic disease.

questions.text: Has any sore, lump, or patch in your mouth lasted longer than two to three weeks?
questions.rationale: Non-healing lesions raise concern for oral cancer and need biopsy evaluation.

questions.text: Have you noticed white or red patches on your tongue, cheeks, or gums that don't wipe off?
questions.rationale: Leukoplakia and erythroplakia are premalignant lesions.

questions.text: Has your tongue changed in color, texture, or sensation, or does it burn?
questions.rationale: Tongue changes may reflect candidiasis, nutritional deficiency, or burning mouth syndrome.

questions.text: Do you have numbness or tingling in your lip, chin, tongue, or face?
questions.rationale: Persistent numbness can indicate nerve involvement from infection, trauma, or tumor.

questions.text: Is your mouth dry, or do you have trouble chewing or swallowing dry food?
questions.rationale: Xerostomia raises caries risk and may relate to medications or Sjogren's disease.

questions.text: Do you have a bad taste, bad breath, or pus draining in your mouth?
questions.rationale: These suggest dental or gum infection or sinus drainage.

questions.text: Did you injure your mouth, teeth, or jaw recently? Is any tooth loose, chipped, or knocked out?
questions.rationale: Dental trauma timing affects whether an avulsed tooth can be saved.

questions.text: Have you had a recent tooth extraction, filling, or other dental procedure?
questions.rationale: Recent procedures raise risk of dry socket, infection, or bleeding.

questions.text: Is there bleeding that won't stop after pressure, or bleeding without a clear cause?
questions.rationale: Persistent oral bleeding may reflect anticoagulation or a bleeding disorder.

questions.text: Do you have jaw pain, clicking, or locking, or grind your teeth at night?
questions.rationale: Jaw symptoms point toward temporomandibular disorder or bruxism.

questions.text: Do you smoke, vape, chew tobacco, or drink alcohol regularly?
questions.rationale: Tobacco and alcohol are the main risk factors for oral cancer.

questions.text: Have you noticed any lumps in your neck or under your jaw?
questions.rationale: Neck nodes can accompany oral infection or malignancy.

questions.text: Have you lost weight, or has it become hard to eat because of the pain?
questions.rationale: Weight loss or poor intake raises urgency and concern for malignancy.

questions.text: Do you take blood thinners, bisphosphonates, steroid inhalers, or medicines that dry your mouth?
questions.rationale: Several drugs affect bleeding, healing, jaw health, or saliva.

questions.text: Do you have diabetes or a weakened immune system?
questions.rationale: These conditions worsen oral infections and slow healing.

questions.text: When did you last see a dentist, and how often do you brush and floss?
questions.rationale: Care history helps frame the likelihood of preventable disease.

questions.text: What is the main thing you are worried this could be?
questions.rationale: Understanding the patient's concern guides reassurance and follow-up questions.

red_flags.label: Lip, tongue, or throat swelling with breathing difficulty
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report swelling of the tongue, lips, or throat, or trouble breathing?

red_flags.label: Facial swelling with trouble swallowing or opening mouth
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report facial or neck swelling together with difficulty swallowing, drooling, or being unable to open the mouth?

red_flags.label: Facial swelling with fever
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report facial or jaw swelling with fever, chills, or feeling very unwell?

red_flags.label: Mouth lesion lasting more than 2 to 3 weeks
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe a sore, lump, or patch in the mouth that has not healed in more than two to three weeks?

red_flags.label: Numbness of lip, chin, or tongue
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report persistent numbness or tingling of the lip, chin, tongue, or face?

red_flags.label: Bleeding that will not stop
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe oral bleeding that continues despite pressure, particularly on blood thinners?

red_flags.label: Knocked-out tooth
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report a tooth that was knocked out or badly displaced in the last few hours?
